reasons: Moving a token to a new user on registration is not checked, so an old account can lose its device.
Unregistering an unknown token raises an error that is not handled.

terms.meaning: an action that updates a record if it exists or creates it if not
one unit of background work placed on the queue

used_by: other modules that send notifications, not shown in this packet

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports, setup and device registration
sections.what: Brings in the queue, the Expo client and database access. Registering a device saves the token for the user, or updates it and marks it active if it already exists.
sections.why: Lets one phone reconnect to a user without creating a duplicate token.
sections.watch_out: A token already saved for another user is reassigned to the new user.

sections.name: NotificationService (part 1)
sections.title: Saving the history record
sections.what: Sends a push notification by first saving a history record with pending status, marked as a push, with the given type.
sections.why: Keeps a record of every notification for the notification history and analytics.
sections.watch_out: The history record is saved before checking devices, so a user with no devices still gets a history entry.

sections.name: NotificationService (part 2)
sections.title: Queuing deliveries and unregistering
sections.what: Finds the user's active devices and queues one delivery job for each with retry settings. If none exist it logs a warning. Unregistering marks a token inactive.
sections.why: Likely reason: one job per device means one bad phone cannot block the others.
sections.watch_out: The unregister call uses a plain update, so an unknown token raises an error that the caller must handle.

summary: Saves a notification to the database, then queues one push delivery job for each active phone the user has, and also stores and updates device push tokens.
purpose: The main entry point other parts of the app use to send a push notification.
why: Likely reason: a queue job per device lets one failing phone be retried without affecting the others.
how: Registering a device saves or updates the token and marks it active. Sending first saves a history record with pending status, finds the user's active devices and queues a delivery job for each. If there are no devices, it logs a warning and returns the record. Unregistering marks the token inactive.
inputs: User id, title, body, optional extra data and notification type, plus device token details.
outputs: The saved notification record, and queued background jobs.
risks: Registration uses the token as the unique key, so a token used by another account is moved to the new user. Unregistering throws an error if the token is unknown.
debug: If a user gets no push, check that the notification record exists, that the user has active devices and that jobs are in the queue. If a token seems to belong to the wrong account, check the registration logic.
